editorial:
Ever felt like you have plenty of people to hang out with, but no one who is actually your best friend? That is exactly where Peter finds himself. He is a great guy with a great fiancée, but once he starts planning his wedding, he realizes he does not have a single male friend he can call his best man. It is a super relatable and awkward setup that leads to some of the funniest scenes you will see in a rom-com. The vibe is light, breezy, and focuses on the struggle of making friends as an adult, which can feel just as scary as dating.

Paul Rudd is perfect here because he brings that natural charm to a character who is trying way too hard. The chemistry between him and Jason Segel is the real highlight, making the weird man-dates feel genuine and hilarious. While some of the jokes are a bit dated, the pacing stays fast and keeps you smiling throughout. It is the kind of easy watch that belongs in your digital collection.
endingExplained: After a big fight where Peter and Sydney drift apart, Peter realizes that true friendship requires honesty and effort. He apologizes and makes things right just in time for the wedding. In the final scenes, Sydney proudly serves as the best man, giving a heartfelt speech that proves they are real best friends. Everything wraps up happily with Peter and Zooey getting married, and the two men remaining close friends for the long haul.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves lighthearted comedies about adult friendships.
